notes.meaning: Jesus tells the people to pay their taxes to the Roman government, but to give their whole hearts and worship to God. Because they used Caesar's coins, they enjoyed the benefits of his civil rule and owed him tax. But since human beings are made in God's image, they belong completely to Him and not to any earthly ruler.

differ.view: God rules through two distinct realms: a worldly kingdom governed by reason and civil law, and a spiritual kingdom where God alone directs the human conscience.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Early church teachers saw giving to God as offering one's own soul, because God's image is stamped on us, as well as giving tithes and sacred offerings.

notes.meaning: The spies sent to trap Jesus could find nothing wrong with what He said in front of the crowd. His wise answer left them astonished and without any charge to bring against Him. Having failed to make Him say something treasonous, they went silent.

Some Sadducees came forward to question Jesus next. They belonged to a wealthy priestly group that rejected the idea that people will ever rise from the dead. They also did not believe in angels, spirits, or any life after death.

The Sadducees reminded Jesus of a command found in the law of Moses. Under that law, if a married man died without children, his brother was required to marry the widow. Any child born from that marriage would carry on the dead brother's name and family inheritance.

To test Jesus, they presented an extreme scenario involving seven brothers. The first brother married a wife and then died without having any children. This left the widow without an heir for her deceased husband.

The second and third brothers married the widow, and one by one all seven brothers took her as a wife and died childless. After all seven had died, the woman died as well. The Sadducees used this exaggerated case to try to make the idea of life after death look completely absurd.

The Sadducees asked whose wife the woman would be when the dead are raised, since all seven brothers had been married to her. They assumed that if there were a resurrection, life in that world would just be a repeat of earthly life. By asking this, they thought they had proven the resurrection to be impossible.

Jesus explains that marriage belongs only to this present earthly age. In this world, people marry and build families to keep the human race going because people die. Earthly marriage serves the needs of mortal human life.

Life in the world to come will be completely different from life right now. Those whom God considers worthy to share in that future age and rise to eternal life will not marry or be given in marriage. Their new life with God will have joys far beyond any earthly bond.

In the resurrection, believers can never die again, which means there is no need for marriage to replace dying generations. They are like the angels because they are immortal and live forever in God's presence. Because they have been raised to everlasting life, their place as children of God is made fully complete.

Jesus proves the resurrection using the books of Moses, the very Scriptures the Sadducees claimed to follow. At the burning bush, the Lord spoke of Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, long after those patriarchs had died. God would not claim to be the God of people who were completely gone and forgotten.

God is not the God of the dead, but of the living, because all who belong to Him remain alive in His presence. Even when believers die on earth, their souls live on with God, and their bodies will one day be raised. God's eternal covenant promises are fulfilled in a life that outlasts the grave.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars propose that the words 'for to Him all are alive' may be an explanatory comment added by Luke to help explain the meaning of Jesus' statement.

notes.meaning: Some of the scribes who were listening spoke up and told Jesus He had answered well. Most scribes were Pharisees who believed in the resurrection, and they were glad to see their theological rivals, the Sadducees, soundly defeated. Even though they opposed Jesus, they had to admit His defense of the Scriptures was brilliant.

After this, none of the religious leaders dared to ask Jesus any more trick questions. Both the Pharisees and the Sadducees had been completely silenced by His wisdom. They realized they could not trap Him with words.

Jesus now takes the initiative and asks a question about the promised Messiah. The religious teachers taught that the Christ would simply be a human descendant of King David. Jesus begins to show them that their view of the Messiah was far too small.

Jesus quotes Psalm 110, where David describes God the Father speaking to David's Lord. God invites the Messiah to sit at His right hand, the place of highest honor and power, until all His enemies are completely brought under His authority. This showed that the Messiah is far greater than an ordinary earthly king.

Jesus presses the puzzle: if David himself calls the Messiah his 'Lord,' how can the Messiah merely be David's son? An ancient father would never call his own descendant his master. The only answer is that the Christ is both: as a human being He came from David's family line, but as God He is David's Lord.

While all the people were listening, Jesus spoke directly to His disciples. He gave His warning in public so that ordinary listeners would not be deceived by corrupt spiritual leaders. True teachers of God must guide people toward humility rather than hypocrisy.

Jesus warns the crowd to watch out for the scribes, who loved to show off their status. They wore long flowing robes to look important, loved respectful greetings in public markets, and took the best seats in synagogues and banquets. Their religion was driven by personal pride and the desire for human praise.

These leaders cheated defenseless widows out of their property while putting on a show of great piety with long, public prayers. Using religion to cover up greed and cruelty is a terrible sin in God's eyes. Because they used God's name to disguise their wicked actions, they will face the harshest judgment.
